findings.issue: The core header block is missing the required `# Sources:` line? No — verify: the core header does contain `# Sources: ...`. Retracted; see summary. Recorded here only as a checked item with no defect.

`committee_members` has range Person[] and is populated with two people whose `id` values are `mailto:` URIs and whose `name` values are derived from email local-parts. `D. Bold` is not stated anywhere in the bundle; the GitHub overview gives only the address `dbold@emory.edu`. The personal name is inferred, not supported. Also, the bundle presents these two addresses as contacts for access requests and general inquiries, not as members of an access-decision committee; the slot's own `source_caveats` admits no committee is described, which makes the population self-contradicting.

Same defect as the full record: inferred personal name `D. Bold` from an email local-part, and use of `committee_members` for contacts the bundle never describes as a committee, contradicted by the object's own `source_caveats`.

Omitted, but the bundle clearly supports a value only in a mixed sense — the dataset spans OMOP relational tables, DICOM images, and waveforms. Omission is defensible; flagged as low-confidence only. Downgrade: not a defect.

`counts: 50000` is asserted as a single integer while the record's own `source_caveats` documents a direct conflict between the webinar (>45,000 unique admissions as of August 2025) and chorus4ai.org (50,000 released admissions). Selecting one figure into a scalar silently resolves a documented source conflict, which the decision rules forbid.
Identical to the full record: scalar `50000` silently selects one side of a conflict the sibling `source_caveats` describes as unresolved.

`counts: 7642` is placed on an instance whose `instance_type` is 'Radiology imaging study extracted from hospital PACS', but 7,642 is the number of *admissions with radiology data*, not the number of imaging studies. The `notes` field acknowledges the mismatch rather than correcting it. The bundle separately states ~1,000 images available. The integer does not count instances of the declared instance type.
Same unit mismatch as the full record: 7,642 counts admissions with radiology data, not imaging studies, while `instance_type` declares imaging studies.

`role` on DataCollector is populated with free-text values ('Data acquisition site', 'Data site manager', 'CHoRUS sub-team'). The schema digest constrains `role` to an enum only on Maintainer, not DataCollector, so this is not a validation failure, but the values are inconsistent in kind with the constrained vocabulary used elsewhere in the same record for the same concept.

`publisher` (range uriorcurie) is set to `https://chorus4ai.org/`, the same value as `id` and `page`. The bundle names no publisher for the dataset; chorus4ai.org is the project website. Using the site URL as a publisher identifier asserts a publisher relationship the bundle does not state.
Same as full: `https://chorus4ai.org/` asserted as publisher with no bundle support, duplicating `id` and `page`.

The Grant object carries only `id: https://reporter.nih.gov/project-details/10472824`, a RePORTER page URL, while the actual grant identifiers the bundle states explicitly (project number 1OT2OD032701-01, core project number OT2OD032701, award amount 5,880,300, project period) are buried in the parent object's free-text `notes`. Declared structured content is placed in prose rather than in the Grant entity.
Same as full: grant number, award amount and project period held in free-text `notes` while the Grant object carries only a page URL as its identifier.

`counts: 1600000000` counts OMOP *rows*, while `instance_type` describes a structured EHR record standardized to OMOP covering five domains. Row count and record count are not the same unit; the `notes` acknowledges rather than reconciles this.
Same unit mismatch as the full record between OMOP row count and the declared instance type.

`created_by` is free text naming the consortium. The bundle supports this, but the value duplicates information already carried structurally in `creators`, and no single creating person or organization is named as primarily responsible in the sources beyond the awardee organization.

`selection_bias` is assigned, but the bundle only states that the project intends to *manage* privacy and bias; it never characterizes an observed bias or identifies its type. The object's own `source_caveats` concedes this. Assigning a specific enum term to an unobserved, uncharacterized bias imputes a categorization the sources do not make.
Same as full: `selection_bias` enum assigned where the bundle characterizes no observed bias, contradicted by the sibling `source_caveats`.

`restricted` is asserted. The bundle states all data types are 'Controlled' access; mapping 'controlled access' onto the enum term `restricted` rather than `confidential` is a judgment the sources do not license explicitly, though `restricted` is the more conservative reading.

Omitted. Correct given the bundle: the MIT License applies to the chorus-ai software repositories, not to the dataset, and `source_caveats` states this reasoning. Recorded as a verified correct omission, not a defect.

All four Maintainer objects use `academic_institution`. For `chorus:maintainer-access-contacts` (two named individuals at Emory and Tufts Medicine) and `chorus:maintainer-developers` (software contributors), `academic_institution` is a poor fit; the enum offers `researcher` and `other`. Uniform assignment flattens distinct maintainer kinds.
Same as full: `academic_institution` applied uniformly to individual contacts and to software contributors.

Contains the email `cmccrary@mgh.havard.edu` transcribed verbatim including the apparent domain typo. The typo is correctly flagged in the top-level `source_caveats`, but embedding an address known to be malformed inside a prose stewardship value propagates an unusable contact without local annotation.

Omitted, though the bundle states '23 Tb' of waveform data. That figure is a modality-specific volume, not a total across all file collections, and no file counts are given, so omission is correct. Recorded as a verified omission.

DataSubset requires only `id`; the object sets `is_data_split: true` and describes the holdout. Consistent with `splits[chorus:split-holdout]`, but the same fact is represented twice in two slots with no cross-reference, which risks divergence on update.

The core record omits both `subsets` and `splits` while retaining the holdout test set in `purposes`, `tasks` and `intended_uses`. The holdout is the dataset's most distinctive structural feature and the projection drops its structured representation entirely.

Present in the full record with `is_direct: false`; absent from the core record. The core omission is unexplained by the projection pattern, since neighbouring Collection-module slots (acquisition_methods, collection_mechanisms, collection_timeframes, data_collectors) are all carried over.

Present in the full record; absent from the core record, while the closely related `is_deidentified`, `sensitive_elements` and `confidential_elements` are all retained in core. Inconsistent projection of the privacy cluster.
Present in the full record (`is_shared: true`); absent from the core record, while `distribution_formats` and `distribution_dates` are retained. Inconsistent projection of the Distribution module.
Omitted in both records. Correct — the bundle states no version identifier, and `source_caveats` says so explicitly. Verified omission.
Omitted in both records. Correct — the bundle provides no DOI and no recommended citation, and `source_caveats` records this. Verified omission.

Omitted. Correct: the bundle describes controlled access via registration and named contacts, not a direct download endpoint, and putting an access route into `download_url` would misuse the slot. Verified omission.

All omitted in both records. The bundle describes retrospective collection from clinical systems and community ethics focus groups but states nothing about individual consent, so omission is correct. Verified omission.

summary: Both records are well grounded in the declared bundle overall, with extensive and generally honest use of source_caveats. Two high-severity defects recur in both records, both in data_governance.committee_members: a personal name ('D. Bold') inferred from an email local-part, and the use of a committee-membership slot for contacts the bundle describes only as access-request addresses — a use the object's own source_caveats explicitly disclaims. A cluster of medium-severity issues concerns Instance.counts, where three of the four populated counts carry units that do not match their declared instance_type (admissions-with-radiology counted as imaging studies, OMOP rows counted as EHR records) or silently resolve a documented source conflict into a scalar (50,000 vs >45,000 admissions). publisher is asserted in both records without bundle support, duplicating the project website URL. Grant structure is under-populated, with the project number, award amount and period held in prose notes while the Grant object carries only a RePORTER page URL. Lower-severity issues include a bias_type enum assigned to an uncharacterized bias, uniform academic_institution roles across heterogeneous maintainers, free-text roles on DataCollector, and propagation of a known-malformed contact email. The core projection is inconsistent rather than wrong: direct_collection, participant_privacy, third_party_sharing, subsets and splits are dropped while closely coupled slots from the same modules are retained, and the holdout test set — the dataset's most distinctive structural feature — loses its structured representation in core. Header blocks, id consistency, conforms_to/conforms_to_standard pairing, enum validity elsewhere, and the many deliberate omissions (license, version, doi, citation, download_url, consent slots) all check out against the bundle.
